sentences.text:
Gulshan Jat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February,
2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:3866
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh
 On The 5 th Of February, 2026
 Criminal Appeal No. 816 of 2026
 Gulshan Jat
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:

Shri Ravindra Singh Chhabra - learned Senior Counsel w
 Akshata Chhabra, counsel for the appellant.

Shri Rajendra Singh Suryavanshi appearing on behalf of
 General[r-1].
 Shri Prabal Jain, learned counsel for the respondent [
 Order

This criminal appeal under Section 14A(2) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 r/w Section 482 of the B.N.S.S., 2023 is preferred being aggrieved by the order dated 14.01.2026 by the Exclusive Special Court designated under SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, Ratlam (M.P.)
whereby an application for releasing of the appellant on anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.972/2025 under Sections 376(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 3(1)(w-ii), 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been rejected.
02.
The appellant/accused and respondent No. 2/prosecutrix were employed in the Madhya P r a d e s h P o l i c e D e p a r t m e n t o n t h e s a m e p o s t . T h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

2026:MPHC-IND:3866 2 CRA-816-2026 prosecutrix belongs to the Scheduled Caste community,
whereas the appellant/accused does not belong to the SC/ST category.

A report was lodged on 29.12.2025 alleging that during the period of 05.11.2018 to 01.03.2021, the appellant/accused established a physical relationship with the prosecutrix on the false promise of marriage.

It is further alleged that thereafter the appellant/accused refused to marry her on the ground that she belongs to the Scheduled Caste community and, thus, he insulted her.
03.

The Trial Court rejected the application on the ground that the appellant/accused has not disclosed the details of his criminal antecedents, as mandated by the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Munnesh vs. State of U.P. , Order dated 03.04.2025 passed in SLP (Criminal) No.
1400/2025.

The Trial Court further observed that the alleged offence is punishable with Gulshan Jat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46047349/
1 imprisonment for life in view of Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and provisions of Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 are attracted in the present case, as the denial of the relationship by the appellant/accused is stated to be continuous till date.
04.

sentences.text: Challenging the impugned order, the present appeal has been preferred on the ground that the case diary itself reflects that the appellant has no criminal antecedents and his criminal record has been recorded as "Nil."
The appellant is presently posted as a Sub-Inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police Department.

Even the matter is considered in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivraj Jain & Ors., AIR 2025 SC 4083 , no prima facie case under the provisions of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3866 3 CRA-816-2026 the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is made out, and consequently, the statutory bar contained under Sections 18 and 18-A of the said Act is not attracted.
05.

entities.text: Kiran v. Rajkumar Jivraj Jain & Ors., AIR 2025 SC 4083
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the appeal.

06. The victim has filed her reply through Document No.1366/2026 alongwith her affidavit through counsel and stated that she does not wish to oppose the anticipatory bail being considered and decided by the Court on merits.

07. On perusal of the contents of the F.I.R., the statement recorded under Section 180 of the BNSS,
2023 and the statement recorded under Section 183 of the BNSS, 2023, the Bar under Section 18 and 18A of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is not attracted in this case.

08. In view of the above, without commenting on the merit of the case, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order is set aside and the appellant is directed to be released on bail subject to his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before that Court, as and when directed, during the pendency of trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under section 480(3) of the BNSS, 2023.
09.
Apart from that, the appellant shall not come in contact with the victim/prosecutrix physically or through any other mode of communication including social media plat form.
If there is any violation of the conditions, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail without reference to this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3866 4 CRA-816-2026 10.

Copy of this order be forwarded to the victim in the light of the judgment in the case of Aparna Bhatt Vs. State of M.P. - AIR 2021 SC 1492.
C.C. as per rules.
